pro_request() - Background and Technical Documentation

Source: vignettes/pro_request.qmd

Introduction

The pro_request() function is the core data retrieval component of the openalexPro workflow. It downloads data from the OpenAlex API and saves it as JSON files to disk, enabling processing of datasets too large to fit in memory.

This vignette provides a comprehensive guide to using pro_request() and related functions, including:

  • Basic usage patterns
  • Progress bars and parallel processing
  • The complete data pipeline (pro_request() → pro_request_parquet())
  • Internal architecture and flow diagrams
  • Error handling and retry logic

Authentication

OpenAlex offers limited API access without credentials. Free API keys with substantially higher rate limits can be obtained from the OpenAlex website. Premium API access with even higher limits can also be purchased.

openalexPro uses environment variables for credentials (recommended):

# Set credentials (typically in your .Renviron file)
Sys.setenv(openalexPro.api_key = "your-api-key-here")

# Validate your credentials
pro_validate_credentials()

You can also pass credentials directly to functions:

pro_request(
  query_url = url,
  output = "data/json",
  api_key = "your-api-key"
)

To force unauthenticated mode for a call, pass api_key = NULL (or ""):

pro_request(
  query_url = url,
  output = "data/json",
  api_key = NULL
)

Basic Usage

Simple Download

The most basic usage requires a query URL (from pro_query()) and an output directory:

library(openalexPro)

# Build query
url <- pro_query(
  entity = "works",
  search = "climate change",
  from_publication_date = "2023-01-01"
)

# Download data
pro_request(
  query_url = url,
  output = "data/json"
)

Get Count Only

To check how many results a query returns without downloading:

# Get count for a single query
count <- pro_request(
  query_url = url,
  count_only = TRUE
)
count$count
# [1] 45632

# Or use pro_count() directly
meta <- pro_count(query_url = url)
meta
#   count db_response_time_ms page per_page error
# 1 45632                  42    1        1    NA

Download with Progress Bar

Progress bars are enabled by default:

pro_request(
  query_url = url,
  output = "data/json",
  progress = TRUE # Default
)
# Downloading ████████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 120/229 [1m 23s]

For a list of queries, the progress bar counts queries; each one advances it in fractions as its pages arrive. No extra count requests are made up front.

Limiting Pages

By default, pro_request() downloads up to 100,000 pages per query (20 million records at 200 per page; pro_fetch() defaults to 10,000 pages). For a list of queries the limit applies to each query. You can adjust this:

# Download only first 100 pages (20,000 records)
pro_request(
  query_url = url,
  output = "data/json",
  pages = 100
)

# Download all pages (use with caution for large queries!)
pro_request(
  query_url = url,
  output = "data/json",
  pages = NULL
)

Handling Chunked Queries

When pro_query() returns a list of URLs (due to automatic chunking of large ID lists), pro_request() handles them seamlessly:

# Query with many DOIs triggers automatic chunking
dois <- paste0("10.1234/example", 1:150)
urls <- pro_query(entity = "works", doi = dois)

length(urls) # 3 chunks
names(urls) # "chunk_1", "chunk_2", "chunk_3"

# pro_request handles the list automatically
pro_request(
  query_url = urls,
  output = "data/json"
)
# Creates: data/json/chunk_1/, data/json/chunk_2/, data/json/chunk_3/

Nested List Queries

pro_request() also accepts nested lists of URLs. Each nesting level is preserved as a subdirectory, and pro_request_parquet() converts the directory depth to hive-style partition keys:

Directory depth Partition key
1 query=<name>
2 query_l2=<name>
3 query_l3=<name> 
# Build a nested query list manually
queries <- list(
  year_2022 = pro_query(entity = "works", publication_year = 2022),
  year_2023 = pro_query(entity = "works", publication_year = 2023),
  institutions = list(
    usa = pro_query(entity = "institutions", country_code = "US"),
    uk  = pro_query(entity = "institutions", country_code = "GB")
  )
)

# Download: creates nested subdirectory structure
pro_request(
  query_url = queries,
  output    = "data/json"
)
# Creates:
#   data/json/year_2022/
#   data/json/year_2023/
#   data/json/institutions/usa/
#   data/json/institutions/uk/

# After parquet conversion the dataset is hive-partitioned:
#   data/parquet/query=year_2022/
#   data/parquet/query=year_2023/
#   data/parquet/query=institutions/query_l2=usa/
#   data/parquet/query=institutions/query_l2=uk/

# Filter by partition
ds <- arrow::open_dataset("data/parquet")
ds |> dplyr::filter(query == "year_2022")
ds |> dplyr::filter(query == "institutions", query_l2 == "usa")

pro_fetch() inherits nested list support automatically — you can pass a nested list directly as query_url.

Parallel Downloads

For chunked queries, enable parallel processing:

pro_request(
  query_url = urls,
  output = "data/json",
  workers = 4 # Use 4 parallel workers
)

Each query is handed to the next free worker, so a few large queries do not leave the other workers idle. Pages within one query are always fetched one after another (by cursor, or by page number for a sample), so workers only helps with a list of queries.

If one query of a list fails (e.g. HTTP 404 for an ID that does not exist), the others still complete. At the end, one error names each failed query with OpenAlex’s reason; resume = TRUE then fetches only those again.

Resuming an Interrupted Download

With resume = TRUE, an existing output is kept and only queries that did not finish are downloaded. Each query directory carries a 00_in.progress marker while it is being written. This works for a single URL as well as for lists, and pro_fetch(resume = TRUE) also completes an interrupted Parquet conversion:

pro_request(query_url = urls, output = "data/json", resume = TRUE)
pro_fetch(query_url = urls, project_folder = "data", resume = TRUE)

Continuing in the middle of a query

An interrupted query does not start again: it continues after its last saved page. OpenAlex’s cursors are positions in the sort order and do not expire, but they contain nothing about the query, so after each page the exact query and the cursor are saved in _paging.json, together with the time the cursor was created:

Resuming `json` at page 4001 with a cursor from 2026-10-14T08:31:48Z
(3.2 hours ago). Records that changed since then may appear twice or be
missing; see `inconsistency_on_resume`. ...

Whatever cannot be trusted – a damaged _paging.json, a different query, missing pages – leads back to fetching the query again from page 1, with a message saying why. Samples and semantic search always start again (they are at most 50 requests). To fetch a query whole on purpose, delete its _paging.json.

Inconsistencies after a resume

Between the sessions OpenAlex’s data can change – citation counts, new works – and records can move across the cursor position: they then appear twice, or are missing. After a resumed query, pro_request() checks:

  • duplicates, exactly, by work ID across all pages of the query;
  • missing records, as the net difference to the number OpenAlex now reports. A record lost and another one added since cancel out, so this check cannot see every gap.

inconsistency_on_resume decides what happens:

Value Duplicates Missing records (net)
"error" (default) stop stop
"warning" keep both copies, warn warn
"ignore" keep both copies –
"oldest" keep the first downloaded copy warn
"newest" keep the last downloaded copy warn

With "error", nothing is lost: everything stays on disk, and a rerun with resume = TRUE and another value applies that choice without downloading anything again. "oldest" and "newest" remove the other copy from its page file. The resume and the result of the check are recorded in the query’s _query.json (resumed, duplicates, duplicates_removed, missing_net, …).

# after an "error": keep the newest copy of each duplicate, no download
pro_request(query_url = urls, output = "data/json", resume = TRUE,
            inconsistency_on_resume = "newest")

Lossless Queries with via = "oqo"

By default every query is sent as a GET request with the query in the URL. With via = "oqo" (also for pro_fetch() and pro_count()), each query is instead translated once into an OpenAlex Query Object (OQO) – the form OpenAlex compiles every query to anyway – and every page is sent as a POST request with the OQO in the body:

pro_fetch(urls, project_folder = "data", via = "oqo")
  • Same results. The test suite downloads the same queries both ways and compares the complete result sets (filters, boolean, wildcard and proximity search, samples, grouped results, other entities, DOI lists, OQL and OQO input). Only semantic search can differ by a work or two – as it does between two identical GET requests.
  • Checked before spending credits. The translation is free and validates the query; an invalid query stops with OpenAlex’s message before any paid request.
  • No URL limits. A URL may carry at most 100 values per filter (with via = "url", pro_request() stops early when a filter has more). An OQO may carry more, so pro_query(..., chunk_limit = 200) fetches a DOI or OpenAlex ID list in about one request per chunk – and the chunks still download in parallel with workers.
  • The exact query is recorded (see below).

Single records (works/W123) are always fetched with GET; they are free.

What Was Asked, and What It Cost

Each query directory gets a _query.json: the URL (without the key), how it was sent (via), the query as OpenAlex ran it (oql, oqo), the number of records, requests and credits, the cost in USD, and when it ran. pro_request_parquet() copies it into the matching Parquet partition, so it is kept when the JSON files are deleted. At the end, pro_request() reports the total, e.g. i 12 requests, 12 credits ($0.0012). Arrow and DuckDB ignore the file (leading underscore, not .parquet).

For methods sections and supplements, each query directory also gets the query in OpenAlex’s readable query language (OQL), in two forms:

  • _query_oql.txt: plain text, ready to paste into a paper, e.g.

    # OpenAlex query (OQL)
# Records: 141 | Downloaded: 2026-10-14 (UTC) | openalexPro 0.13.0
# Exact: this OQL translates back to exactly the query that ran.

get works where full text has (microbio*)
  and source is [Nature](S137773608)
  and published in 2020

  • _query_oql.html: the same, nicely formatted with highlighted keywords and OpenAlex IDs linked to their records; self-contained (no scripts, no external resources), with the exact OQO and the request URL in collapsible sections.

The OQL is OpenAlex’s own rendering of the query that ran. Because that rendering can be lossy in some details, it is translated back and compared: the header says Exact if the printed OQL reproduces the query, otherwise Not exact (then the OQO in _query.json is the exact query) or Not checked (if OpenAlex’s free /query endpoint could not be reached). Single records (works/W123) get no OQL files. Like _query.json, both files are copied into the Parquet partition.

For a list of queries, _queries_oql.txt and _queries_oql.html at the top of the output summarise all queries for a supplement: in the order of the list, each query’s name, number of records, whether its OQL is exact, and the OQL itself, with totals (records, credits, cost) in the header; the HTML adds an overview table linking to each query. Queries skipped by resume = TRUE are included, failed ones are listed as “Not downloaded”. Both files are copied to the top of the Parquet folder.

The API key is sent as an Authorization: Bearer header, never in the URL, so it does not appear in logs, error messages or recorded test responses.

Function Parameters Reference

Parameter Type Default Description
query_url character/list required URL or list of URLs from pro_query()
pages integer/NULL 100000 Max pages per query. NULL = all pages
output character required Directory for JSON output files
overwrite logical FALSE Delete existing output directory if it exists
api_key character/NULL env var Optional API key. If NULL or "", requests are sent without key.
workers integer 1 Parallel workers for list queries
verbose logical FALSE Show detailed messages
progress logical TRUE Show progress bar
count_only logical FALSE Return count without downloading
error_log character/NULL NULL Path for error log file
resume logical FALSE Keep output, refetch only unfinished queries
via character “url” "url" (GET) or "oqo" (translated once, sent via POST)

pro_request() Architecture

High-Level Flow

fetch_query_pages() Internal Helper

The fetch_query_pages() function handles the actual page-by-page download:

Whether a query is grouped is decided from the first response (grouped responses carry a numeric meta$groups_count), not from the URL, so grouping inside an OQL / OQO query is detected as well. Grouped pages are saved as group_by_page_N.json.

api_call() Retry Logic

All HTTP requests go through api_call() which provides robust retry logic. Network failures (dropped connection, curl errors) are retried like transient statuses, and a transfer that stalls (less than 1 byte/s for 120 s) is aborted and retried. A 429 caused by the daily budget is not retried (see below):

Transient Error Handling

The following HTTP status codes are considered transient and trigger automatic retry:

Status Meaning Action
429 Too Many Requests (more than 100 requests/s) Wait with exponential backoff
500 Internal Server Error Retry up to 10 times
502 Bad Gateway Retry up to 10 times
503 Service Unavailable Retry up to 10 times
504 Gateway Timeout Retry up to 10 times

Not retried, because retrying cannot help:

Status Meaning Behaviour
429 Daily budget used up (X-RateLimit-Remaining is 0), or not_enough_credits (the query costs more than is left) Abort at once; the error says when the budget resets (midnight UTC)
400, 403, 404 Invalid query, no access, not found Abort; the error includes OpenAlex’s own message, e.g. which filter name is invalid, or the OQL parse error

Output File Structure

After a successful download, the output directory contains:

data/json/
├── results_page_1.json
├── results_page_2.json
├── results_page_3.json
└── ...

For chunked queries (list of URLs):

data/json/
├── chunk_1/
│   ├── results_page_1.json
│   ├── results_page_2.json
│   └── ...
├── chunk_2/
│   ├── results_page_1.json
│   └── ...
└── chunk_3/
    └── ...

Progress Tracking

During download, a 00_in.progress file exists in the output directory. This file is automatically deleted upon successful completion. If present, it indicates:

  • Download is still in progress, OR
  • Download was interrupted and is incomplete

resume = TRUE uses this marker to decide which queries to fetch again.

The Complete Data Pipeline

Pipeline Overview

pro_fetch() runs steps 2 and 3 in one call.

Complete Example 

library(openalexPro)

# Step 1: Build query
urls <- pro_query(
  entity = "works",
  search = "machine learning healthcare",
  from_publication_date = "2020-01-01",
  type = "article",
  select = c(
    "ids", "title", "abstract_inverted_index", "publication_year",
    "authorships", "cited_by_count"
  )
)

# Step 2: Download JSON from API
pro_request(
  query_url = urls,
  output = "data/json",
  pages = 1000,
  progress = TRUE
)

# Step 3: Convert to Parquet (adds `abstract` and `citation` columns)
pro_request_parquet(
  input_json = "data/json",
  output = "data/parquet",
  progress = TRUE,
  workers = 4
)

# Step 4: Query with DuckDB
library(duckdb)
con <- dbConnect(duckdb())
dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "
  SELECT title, publication_year, cited_by_count
  FROM read_parquet('data/parquet/**/*.parquet')
  ORDER BY cited_by_count DESC
  LIMIT 10
"
)

pro_request_parquet()

Purpose

Converts the JSON files written by pro_request() into an Apache Parquet dataset using DuckDB, one Parquet file per JSON file, with no intermediate files. During conversion it:

  1. Reconstructs abstracts from abstract_inverted_index (column abstract)
  2. Generates citation strings such as “Smith et al. (2023)” (column citation)
  3. Adds a page column for tracking data provenance
  4. Optionally adds constant columns (add_columns)

Abstracts and citations are only added for works, when the needed fields are present and enrich = TRUE (the default). pro_fetch() calls pro_request() and then pro_request_parquet().

Function Signature 

pro_request_parquet(
  input_json = NULL,
  output = NULL,
  add_columns = list(),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  progress = TRUE,
  delete_input = FALSE,
  sample_size = 1000,
  workers = NULL,
  enrich = TRUE,
  schema = "auto",
  resume = FALSE,
  on_error = c("error", "warn", "ignore"),
  memory_limit = NULL,
  retry_memory_limit = NULL
)

Parameters

Parameter Type Default Description
input_json character required Directory of JSON files from pro_request()
output character required Output directory for the Parquet dataset
add_columns list list() Named character scalars added as constant columns
overwrite logical FALSE Overwrite an existing output
verbose logical TRUE Show progress messages
progress logical TRUE Show a progress bar
delete_input logical FALSE Delete input_json after a complete conversion (kept if any file failed)
sample_size integer 1000 Records per file sampled for schema inference (-1 = all)
workers integer/NULL NULL Parallel workers; NULL or 1 runs sequentially
enrich logical TRUE Add abstract and citation columns for works
schema character/NULL “auto” Baseline schema for ambiguous column types (see below)
resume logical FALSE Keep output and convert only missing files
on_error character “error” What to do with files that still fail: "error", "warn", "ignore"
memory_limit character/NULL NULL DuckDB memory limit per worker; derived from RAM and workers
retry_memory_limit character/NULL NULL Memory limit for the sequential retry pass

Internal Flow

Schema Harmonization

Different OpenAlex records can have different field structures. For example:

  • A field can be a struct in one record and null in all records of another page
  • Nested arrays can be empty in one file and populated in another

pro_request_parquet() therefore infers one schema from a sample of up to 20 files (sample_size records per file) and converts every file with these column types, so all Parquet files can be read together:

When DuckDB can only infer the generic JSON type for a column (for example because it is null in every sampled record), the schema argument supplies the type:

  • "auto" (default): detect the entity from the columns and use the matching baseline schema from the user cache (oa_schema(update = TRUE)) or the schemas bundled with the package
  • "none" or NULL: use DuckDB’s inference only
  • a CSV file (columns col_name, col_type) or a directory of <entity>.csv files

Failure Handling and Resume

Each file is converted on its own, so one problematic page does not stop the others:

  • Every file is written to a .part sidecar and renamed only on success, so a Parquet file that exists is always complete.
  • With workers > 1, files that fail (typically from memory pressure on large, deeply nested pages) are retried once, sequentially and with the whole memory budget.
  • Files that still fail are handled according to on_error: "error" (default) stops and names them, "warn" warns and returns, "ignore" is silent. In every case the JSON input is kept and 00_in.progress stays in output.
  • resume = TRUE keeps an existing output and converts only the files that are missing:
pro_request_parquet(
  input_json = "data/json",
  output = "data/parquet",
  resume = TRUE
)

With workers > 1, each worker gets its own DuckDB connection with a share of the memory budget, one thread and a private temporary directory.

Output Structure

For a flat (single-URL) input:

data/parquet/
├── results_page_1.parquet
├── results_page_2.parquet
└── ...

For a flat list of URLs (e.g. chunk_1, chunk_2 from auto-chunking):

data/parquet/
├── query=chunk_1/
│   ├── results_page_1.parquet
│   └── results_page_2.parquet
└── query=chunk_2/
    └── results_page_1.parquet

For a two-level nested list:

data/parquet/
├── query=year_2022/
│   └── results_page_1.parquet
├── query=year_2023/
│   └── results_page_1.parquet
└── query=institutions/
    ├── query_l2=usa/
    │   └── results_page_1.parquet
    └── query_l2=uk/
        └── results_page_1.parquet

The hive partition columns (query, query_l2, …) become regular columns when you open the dataset with arrow::open_dataset(), enabling efficient predicate pushdown.

Deprecated: the JSONL Pipeline

pro_request_jsonl() and pro_request_jsonl_parquet() converted the JSON files in two steps via intermediate JSONL files. They still work but are deprecated; pro_request_parquet() replaces both. See their help pages (?pro_request_jsonl, ?pro_request_jsonl_parquet) for existing code.

Error Handling

Common Errors

Output Directory Exists 

pro_request(query_url = url, output = "data/json")
# Error: Directory data/json exists.
# Either specify `overwrite = TRUE` or delete it.

# Solution:
pro_request(query_url = url, output = "data/json", overwrite = TRUE)

No Output Specified 

pro_request(query_url = url)
# Error: No `output` specified!

API Rate Limiting

OpenAlex allows up to 100 requests per second and a daily budget ($0.10 without an API key, $1 with a free key). If you exceed the per-second limit (HTTP 429), the function retries with exponential backoff. If the daily budget is used up, it stops at once and reports when the budget resets (midnight UTC). To stay within the budget:

  1. Use an API key (free from OpenAlex)
  2. Check the cost first: searches cost ten times as much as filter queries
  3. Use resume = TRUE after the reset to complete an interrupted download

You can check your current budget and remaining allowance at any time with:

pro_rate_limit_status()

This queries the /rate-limit endpoint and prints your daily budget, amount used, remaining balance, and seconds until the daily reset.

Request Size Exceeded

OpenAlex has a maximum request size of 4094 characters. If exceeded:

meta <- pro_count(query_url = very_long_url)
meta$count
# [1] -4195  # Negative indicates error

meta$error
# [1] "ERROR: Request size exceeds the maximum limit of 4094."

Solution: Use pro_query() with chunking (it handles this automatically).

Best Practices

1. Always Use Progress Bars

Progress bars help monitor long downloads and estimate completion:

pro_request(url, output = "data", progress = TRUE)

2. Use Appropriate Page Limits

Start with smaller page limits during development:

# Development: small sample
pro_request(url, output = "test", pages = 10)

# Production: full download
pro_request(url, output = "data", pages = 10000)

3. Enable Error Logging for Large Jobs 

pro_request(
  query_url = urls,
  output = "data/json",
  error_log = "download_errors.log"
)

4. Clean Up Intermediate Files

Use delete_input = TRUE to save disk space:

# Convert and delete JSON (kept if any file failed to convert)
pro_request_parquet(
  input_json = "data/json",
  output = "data/parquet",
  delete_input = TRUE
)

pro_fetch() deletes the JSON files by default (delete_input = TRUE).

5. Use Parallel Processing Wisely

More workers isn’t always better:

# Downloads: limited by the API, a few workers for a list of queries
pro_request(urls, output = "data/json", workers = 4)

# Conversion: CPU and memory bound; each worker gets a share of the memory
pro_request_parquet("data/json", "data/parquet", workers = parallel::detectCores() - 1)

# pro_fetch() does both: `download_workers` for the download (defaults to
# `workers`), `workers` for the conversion
pro_fetch(urls, project_folder = "data", download_workers = 4,
          workers = parallel::detectCores() - 1)
